notes.title: Lepioid Update: Been a bit!
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! It's been a while, hasn't it?

I hope everyone's been enjoying the game in its current state! Honestly, this silly lil' idle game did much better than I ever thought it would. Thanks!
but that begs the question...what have I been up to in the meantime? What about the game? Will X bugs ever be fixed????

What has Lepioid LLC been doing?
if the game hasn't been updated, what have I been doing? Well, recently, I got together with some cool friends and made another game: Dreams of Aether! It's a fun little microgame collection that was a blast to work on. Check it out here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3463050/Dreams_of_Aether/

Once we got that all finished, I kinda had to take a break from gamedev, haha. It was kind of a marathon! But obviously I'd never stay away forever, so I'm looking to get back into the thick of it. Make some new things, update some old things, all that fun stuff.

What about Settlemoon?
I think Settlemoon's pretty...setttled at this point! It's got a good amount of content and it's MOSTLY smoothed out. (i'll get to that in a bit.) I do have a lot of stuff that I think could be changed about the weird idle-townbuilder formula, but I think that's something better saved for a sequel or spiritual successor. Believe me, there's a LOT of stuff behind the scenes that I wanna do with Settlemoon's world, still.

Also, I have an Android port in the works! It's in a PRETTY good state but I'd still need to confirm everything on the port works and finalize everything on the storefront and legal end. When I think it's ready to release, I'll let you guys know! 

Bug fixes?
I'm aware of some rare bugs that are pretty game-ruining! Unfortunately due to the rarity and how much of the game's effects take time to happen, it's really hard to reproduce anything. I'm still gonna take measures to fix them, though! Here's what I'm planning:

 Much more robust save backups
 Better file management (manual backups and file select)
 Failsafe for getting stuck on "catching up..."


The actual timeframe of fixing these I'm not entirely sure of yet; unfortunately bugfixes are something that take a mysterious amount of time. So for now I'm chalking it up to "soon(tm)".


That's everything for now! Thanks for reading this, and again, thanks for sticking with my silly lil' game for so long!

notes.title: v2.4a - Small hotfix for boss quests
notes.notes:
Hello again!

Tiny fix. Teeny fix. Probably not going to be the only fix. You know how these things go.

QUESTS:

 Fixed a crash when attempting to pay for a boss quest.
 Added a failsafe if you somehow don't get the milestone for a boss clear the first time; it'll now attempt to re-unlock it every time you pay for the quest.

notes.title: v2.3a - Building Removal Hotfix
notes.notes:
Hello! Just some quick fixes for some pretty important things. Deleting buildings permanently is pretty bad.

BUILDINGS:

 Fixed buildings not going back into storage when you remove them with another building.
 Fixed the ferris wheel leaving behind the base when removed via the renovator. (It was actually left behind when you delete it normally, just invisible. Whoops!)
 Fixed the phonograph not being solid.
 When the town is renovating, the camera only moves to the newest building's position when it's offscreen.

notes.title: v2.3 - The Renovator Update
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! This update's got some very highly sought-after improvements for how building things works. 

Most notably, Decorations have had a huge rebalancing. They're now a lot stronger and more interesting to place down; As a decor takes up more space, the range it reaches gets further while the boost it provides gets weaker. This means you can get a LOT of decor overlapping one building to supercharge it.

Not only that, there's now what I call the Town Renovator! You now have three little snow globes in the buildings menu. Using one of these will swap out your ENTIRE town with whatever you have already stored in there. It's a really fast way to change your town's layout, or just bulldoze everything and try something new.

That's the most notable changes, but there's more than that! Here's the full patch notes:

BUILDINGS (Features):

 Added a Town Renovator! You can swap out your town layout using 3 different slots, letting you quickly clear out or change up your town.
 Added a phonograph. It's buildable late in NG+ and plays a certain someone's tracks after their work is done.
 Attempting to place a building over multiple others now stores all overlapping ones (and you still pick up the closest one)
 A couple more decorations are now paintable. (Boss 4's table and candle, as well as some seasonal decor)
 Added a secret to a building. (Hint: Bubble)
 Pawn shops now offer stacks of 5 materials instead of single materials, making them more worth it for the real estate.
 Warehouses now accept up to 12 sellable items and will attempt to distribute them to refill stores as well as materials.



BUILDINGS (Adjustments):

 Buffed overall decor range and strength. Now as a general guideline, the more space the decor takes up, the larger its range gets while the weaker its boost gets. There's a couple exceptions though to keep some interesting niches.

notes.title: v2.2 - The One Year Anniversary Update!
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! It's been one whole year since the game first released, and I couldn't be happier with how everything has gone.

To celebrate, we've updated the game with some anniversary-related things, as well as some good old quality-of-life to hopefully make the early parts of the game easier and less...confusing. Maybe on my next game I should just explain everything with text, haha.

BUILDINGS:

 Added 3 new floor types: Brick, Quilt and Classic Rock
 Added an anniversary shop! Sells random fireworks and a party hat.
 Added a new set of decor! Things hanging on ropes, a new late-game flower, and a FIRE JET. Normal stuff.
 Increased capacity per-item of Warehouses, 99 -> 999
 Fixed the Incinerator not being solid.
 Fixed a Hitching Post decor being buried in the ground.


PROGRESSION:

 Some old envelopes have appeared in the menus...They point out the basics of how each menu works. They show up as a hint button on those menus as well, so you can turn that off in the options.
 Added more steps to the town expansion so that little task starts much earlier. There's now a trinket associated with it! If you're loading an old save file, it'll consider those already done.


ADVENTURERS:

 Added 5 new hats and 5 new heads.
 Adventurers have a chance to be very color-coordinated...what do you think determines that?


MENUS:

 Added a rapid click function for the Materials menu; you can now hold rapid click to stack up mats EXTREMELY fast.
 Added more clarification to the Decor hint card.

notes.title: v2.1b - Small NG+/Building hotfix
notes.notes:
Hello again, Catalysts! Very small hotfix today for some pretty important bugs.

BUGFIXES:

 Fixed a crash that happens when first starting NG+.
 Fixed buildings becoming intangible if you cancel moving one.

notes.title: v2.1 - The Very Useful Things update
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! Pretty big update! New buildings, new cards, and a WHOLE lot of little tweaks here and there to make things smoother. If you're playing on the Steam Deck, everything should properly adapt to it now!

Also important is a controls menu! Wow! I'm so adamant on developers adding these, yet I didn't add one to my own game. How hypocritical...UNTIL NOW.

PROGRESSION:

 Added a Rabbit & Steel cameo! It should show up after Boss 3 becomes available.
 Added Hint Cards that you get as you progress through the game. These should have (still cryptic) hints on how some mechanics work.
 (hopefully) fixed the ending not accounting for placed buildings.
 Most cards you get are now non-dismissable until you get to the end of them.
 Fixed the tutorial card re-view on the main menu playing the unlock animation.


BUILDINGS:

 Added a Warehouse! These evenly distribute materials you put in them across town, refilling shop stocks.
 Added an Incinerator! These burn up materials and items for a small amount of extra time to the current night.
 Added a Grill! It's a lategame variant of the Bakery, though it's not a lot of overlap.
 New Decor! A popcorn machine, hitching post, tacky lightup arrow sign, and more!
 Clocks now have standard decor properties.
 The signal catcher now works a little differently. Once it gets a signal, you hold click on it for a second. After you do that, then it sets ALL elements to 0 and unlocks the signal.
 T2 class shops have had their attract rates slightly buffed.
 Moths no longer push out of each other if they're past the town borders, so hopefully they don't push out of the screen.
 Geode Shops now create a Rock Bag out of 100 pebbles...that sells for as much as 100 pebbles.
 Boss 5's material now makes a new item in T1 class shops.


ADVENTURERS:

 Optimized offscreen adventurers; they don't update every frame now.
 Fixed NPCs holding the wrong card if new cards were added after they spawned (again).
 Fixed adventurers walking in place.
 Picking up an adventurer while stock displays are open now shows some stats about them and what they've bought.



UI:

 Added a Controls menu! You can now rebind your controls. Yay!
 The options button is now darker on the title screen so as to be less eye-catching during the intro.
 Made various improvements to how controllers handle.
 The cursor now snaps to "ENTER WORLD" on controller so you can get in real fast.
 Changed how cameo cards look to be a little cooler.
 Popup menus now have a nice little animation when they spawn.
 There's now a Button Magnifier option. With it enabled, it shows a much larger number when stacking up resources.
 Fixed grabbing menus if you're already holding the mouse down.
 the "Reset Default Options" button in submenus now only resets the options present in that submenu.
 The cursor now shows an indicator when scrolling.


COMPATABILITY:

 The game now always starts in fullscreen when in Big Picture Mode.
 Fullscreen and window size options no longer appear when on the Steam Deck or other fullscreen-only platforms.
 The tutorial's control prompts now adapt to the type of control scheme you're using.
 Steam deck and Big Picture Mode now display virtual keyboards when renaming a friend.
 Added A+X as a default binding for rapid click on controllers.


QUESTS:

 Boss quests are now limited to 300 completions to keep save file sizes consistent.
 Fixed being able to add materials to a completed fetch quest.
 Increased ice nautilus drops: 6 ice 3 shell -> 10 ice 6 shell
 Increased pillow drops: 4 silk 6 feather -> 8 silk 8 feather
 Applied save compression to the quests file. You shouldn't notice anything, but still worth noting!



WORLD:

 Added several new rare moon variants.
 Fixed some names.

notes.title: v2.0e - The shovel hotfix
notes.notes:
Hello, excavating Catalysts! Do you like shovels? Do you like shovels that don't break? Then this update is for you.

SHOVEL:

 Fixed picking up invisible buttons when using the shovel.
 Adjusted the final photo of the shovel sidequest.
 Made a couple of the shovel spots easier to hit.
 Fixed a crash when double-clicking the shovel.
 Fixed a crash when trying to pick up a material while holding the shovel and vice versa.
 The shovel.

notes.title: v2.0c - Fast lil crash hotfix!
notes.notes:
Hello again, Catalysts!! Very small fast hotfix for this; we were getting reports of a very strange crash. Remember when I said "Everything's proooobably okay"? Turns out that wasn't entirely true, haha. We'll be keeping an eye out on any other issues.

THE ONLY PATCH NOTE:

 Fixed a crash on load when a cocoon attempted to spawn.

notes.title: v2.0b - The "moths make noises now" update
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! Nice lil' QoL and bugfix patch here. Most notably, moths and beetles make NOISES when you click them now. Hopefully that's not too startling!
Also, that "New Discoveries" tab's weird behavior is fixed. It shouldn't send you into an empty menu anymore.

Also changed a bunch of stuff under the hood that SHOULDN'T affect anything. Everything's proooobably okay.

BUILDINGS:

 Clickable town-things (moths, shrines) no longer react on certain menus. (buildings and visitors)
 Moths and Beetles now make noises when you click them.
 Fixed some missing item names in the geode shop.


MENUS:

 Materials and Item menus now support rapid-click: hold it down and sweep over the buttons to grab a sampling of all of them
 Fixed the "New Discoveries" building filters locking you in an empty buildings menu.
 The building filters menu now updates live as buildings are marked as seen.
 Changed the name of the "Shops" menu to "Utility" to be more accurate.
 Added some missing building filter names.
 Fixed menus lagging behind by 1 frame (i think this was caused by a gamemaker update)
 Fixed a crash when rearranging friends that are in a guild.
 Holding a shovel now hides boss arenas and makes voids transparent.


PROGRESSION:

 Fixed the NG+ tutorial having a softlock with checking if you have enough resources to build an Inn.
 Fixed the NG+ intro screen putting the score tally on the wrong layer. It now appears behind the menu.
 Fixed prestiging not tallying anything up (that was broken???)
 Fixed Sidequest 2 starting in the wrong state until something refreshes it.
 Fixed Sidequest 6 not properly setting the state of quests.

notes.title: v2.0a - NG+ Hotfix
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! Small hotfix for some things that could stall things out in NG+ as well as a couple other things that snuck in. No categories this time, not really enough notes for that. (heehee)


 Fixed an unruly cooldown timer on NG+ NPC appearances.
 Fixed some unnamed items.
 Fixed the rapid click hotkey buzzing when holding it over an empty button.

notes.title: The New Moon+ Update is Here!
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! Version 2.0, The New Moon+ Update, is finally here! This update adds a whole bunch of new things to do once everything's all done and you start NG+. There's also a bunch of QoL and bugfixes to smooth things out regardless of how much you've progressed.

The New Moon+ stuff puts a twist on the usual mechanics you've gotten used to over the course of the game. Perform alchemy, build rides and do more weird stuff! Complete these side-objectives and you'll learn more about Settlemoon's history and inner workings.

If you've got a town in late-game NG+, I'd GENTLY recommend waiting until your next loop to start the new content. It's not necessary, though! You'll just have a real big head-start on the new content due to having a bunch of bosses beaten and stacks of resources. It might be a little overwhelming!


For a more detailed FAQ on starting this update, check out this thread in Discussions.

Patch notes:

HIGHLIGHTS

 NG+ STORYLINE ADDED! There is now a variety of new things added to NG+ runs. Existing towns in NG+ will also get this content over time, but I softly recommend trying it on a new loop.
 Added new Steam achievements for NG+.


ADVENTURERS

 Adventurers can now spawn with uncommon Back cosmetics. Wings and tails!
 Adventurers have a very rare chance to drop in.
 Adventurers that are leaving town can now be flung into the sky and off the sides.
 Fixed NPCs being unable to spawn on the right side of town.
 Fixed adventurers walking on air. (sorry)
 Once a minute, a low-level adventurer will leave and be replaced by another low-level.


BUILDINGS

 Added a Geode Shop! Take a chance with your excess rocks.
 The rest of the elemental shrines have been given proper recipes.
 Fixed Guildmembers not levelling up if they aren't friends.
 When deciding quests, Guildmembers now consider the classes of all of their comrades too.
 While guilds will prefer certain quest types, they'll still have a chance of taking unfitting options.
 Shrines now constantly release a slow stream of particle effects.


ITEMS

 Adventurers now have a chance to buy the default item if a shop's inventory is small enough. 
 Adjusted endgame item stats to not be so ridiculous.
 Adjusted how item stats contribute to the world to make them decay faster overall.


MENUS

 Added (optional) Scroll Bars to menus!
 Friends and quests now wait for you to stop swiping before being counted as dragged off.
 Resource buttons in the Visitors menu now display a negative amount of money, to be consistent with quests.
 Storycards now display things that they unlock.
 Pressing Back (escape, backspace, etc.) when menus are closed prompts you to close the game.
 The World Map now changes color according to the current event.
 Added a new *experimental* keybind: Holding both Left click and Right click while on the Visitors menu lets you sweep across the screen and buy any material you hover over.


QUESTS

 Reworked how adventurers decide on quests to act like more of a weighted list. 
 Monsters now attempt to move out of the way of Boss buttons.
 Fixed monster quests being overly-preferred by every class.
 Class lights on quests are now hidden until you beat the Eye Stalker.
 The moth that appears on uncleared bosses now better adapts its color to the boss. Yay!


WORLD

 Added Silver Beetles! They spawn in empty spaces and fly away after a few minutes, but if you manage to click on them you get 50 silver. This should help out early game.
 Melee and Ranged cocoons now spawn unique moths, which temporarily change the normal moon to slight variants.
 An odd constellation appears at the start of a new run...
 The language now makes sense. Good luck!
 Fixed dead cocoons saving as live moths.


TUTORIAL

 The Town guide has been reworked to be a lot more descriptive.
 When stocking the inn for the first time, the guide moth now flies to the TOP of the inn.
 The tutorial now skips the step where you have to double click a building to open its stock.
 The tutorial now has a step that forces the Buildings menu to the Shops category.



ALSO

 Revamped controller support. The Left stick now moves freely while the Dpad attempts to snap to buttons.
 Fixed the NG+ ending cutscene having a jarring cutoff on super-widescreen windows.

notes.title: The New Moon+ Update releases March 25th!
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=F5WmqWhC_VU;full][/previewyoutube]

It's almost here!! Woohoo!!

The New Moon+ Update (formerly "new moon part 2") is a BIG update for Settlemoon that puts an entire new spin on New Game+ runs. New useful buildings, new goals to hit, and new cards to collect! It's like playing the game all over again! 

All you'll need to do to see all of this new cool story content is to beat the game at least once. A new NPC will arrive in your town to kick things off. While I'd softly recommend trying this content in tandem with a new NG+ (or even NG+++++) playthrough, you can delve into the new stuff even if your town is in an endgame state.

This new storyline will put a bunch of twists to the usual town-building and quest-posting formula. Good luck trying to fit everything! Maybe you'll be able to find some extra practical uses for all the new stuff you get...

Even if you haven't beaten the game yet, there will still be plenty of Quality-of-Life fixes to help smooth things out! Stuff like quests, guild halls and menu navigation have all seen some improvements.

See you on March 25th! The next full moon!

notes.title: New Moon Update (Part 1) Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts!

It's time, it's time! Time for the New Moon update.....PART 1.

Yeah, remember when I said the update has two parts? And how I wanted to release it before the end of the year? Yeah i actually split it up into two updates. I suppose this one could be called the..."almost new moon, but still kind of a waning crescent" update.

This update focuses on a smoother first experience. Obscure mechanics like item stats, guilds and cocoons should be easier to interpret now, and there should be fewer points where the player doesn't know what to do next. Of course, we'll be keeping an eye on it to see if it sticks the landing and making further adjustments on what doesn't.

Part 2 of the update will focus on adding a ton of stuff to NG+ runs! I've talked about it on another post already so I won't repeat much. You can see what I said about it here.
That part of the update will definitely be in early 2024.

Also in this update is a special little cameo from Cobalt Core! You'll get it once the Level 50 boss introduces themselves. That's the second cameo appearance in this game, along with Familiars.io!

ADVENTURERS:

 Added plenty of new adventurer cosmetic options.
 Friend cards have now been visually reworked to take up less space.
 Friend codes have been updated to be thinner and envelop the name in brackets too. (old ones still work.)
 Soldiers can now learn a way to not faceplant.
 Adventurers can now discuss the latest trends.
 Shepherds can now buy mushroom tomes.
 Gordo has arrived.
 During the opening, a certain moth appears more often...
 Low-level adventurers leave much faster, speeding up early game.
 If there are no adventurers in town with the sky lit, it will spawn a random adventurer to keep you company.
 Certain NPCs spawning will now have a much shorter cooldown for the next NPC spawning.
 Increased spawn chance of crossover-giving mailmanteaters.


PROGRESSION:

 Stocking the inn during the tutorial will summon a lot of adventurers to it.
 Bosses now show up at lower levels.
 Increased starting silver, 600 -> 2000
 The starting quest now finishes in 10 seconds instead of 1 minute.
 The starting quest now gives some Stone and Fireballs too.
 Finishing the starting quest now spawns double the monsters on the map.
 The Merchant achievement now checks for Inns too.


QUESTS:

 Halved resources, cost and time for some beginning monsters so they act more piecemeal.
 Drastically sped up monster spawn rate; 15 minutes -> 5 minutes


BUILDINGS:

 Refined effects when items are bought, to (hopefully) make their effects clearer.
 Magic shops now have icons for their elements.
 Buffed training area boosts, 2 -> 4
 Added plenty of new decor: Chess pieces, topiary, balloons...
 Added event variants of guild halls!
 Guild halls now display some extra info, clarifying their purpose.


WORLD:

 Leafy cocoons are now starry...
 Leafy cocoons will now become "branded" when close to hatching, locking it in.
 Leafy cocoons now determine its outcome via a total of all influencing factors while it was pupating, not just the most prominent at the end.
 Starting a new moon will summon a burst of adventurers depending on your town level.
 Constellations now appear in the sky...
 A cameo from Cobalt Core and Sunshine Heavy Industries has appeared! It'll show up soon after the Lv. 50 boss introduces themselves.


MENUS:

 The buildings menu now has a filter for new buildings.
 The buildings menu now turns on both new and highlight buildings when one is in both categories.
 Fixed touchscreens not registering taps on a menu occasionally.
 The NG+ building category has been moved closer to the center of the list.
 The options menu has been split up into several sub-menus to reduce clutter.
 Added options for fullscreen and saving/reseting window size.


OTHER:

 Corrected a background sprite in the ending.
 Some other materials are now floaty.
 Fixed the Excavator achievement not unlocking in rare cases.
 Deleting your save file should now be more thorough.
 Did a lot of behind the scenes setup for Part 2. Nothing noticable yet...

notes.title: Sneak peek at the next update
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! Here's a little sneak peek into what's next for Settlemoon.

We're working on a really big content update!! So big in fact that it's worth actually naming:
The New Moon update.
This update has two big parts: A big chunk of stuff to do for people who've already beaten the game, and one that makes confusing bits a lot easier to understand.

First: The content update! I don't want to reveal EVERYthing in this update, so for now...
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44164046/1b8bbcdbbf852effe922a479943d95ba7e8677ba.gif
The majority of stuff added in this update will be exclusive to NG+ runs. If it's your first time through, you won't encounter these. And with good reason; there'll be a lot of twists to existing mechanics that would be pretty tough to figure out if you aren't already familiar with them. It's an odd sort of hard mode, I suppose!
Of course, if you want to just ignore all the new weird stuff and replay the game as if it's the first run again, you can do that too.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44164046/eb2f238d985bf194b6efb7eec515bb173f45284b.png
If this is your first run through the game, there'll be some interesting changes before you beat it, too! This set of changes is mostly to make it easier to understand what's going on behind the scenes. Mostly in regards to what those funny little symbols on some items mean, but we're also going to make the opening hours much easier to get through, so you don't just stall out frame 1.

This isn't a game meant to be binged or anything (go to bed!!), but being immediately hit with a requirement to just close the game for a few hours can definitely be a turn-off. That tends to happen way later in most other idlers, but in Settlemoon it's a part of the core game loop; we'd like to make it feel less jarring and a bit more natural for the player to transition to the stage of the game where you want for the town to do its own thing for a little bit before opening it back up.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44164046/98775a4f6d7e9583d39cf8f51621639393b1ed81.gif
Thanks for checking this out! I'd LIKE to get this update out before the end of the year, but I think it's too early to give an actual date. Thanks for your patience regardless! This year has been nuts with other game releases anyway.

notes.title: v1.6e - Cloud save loading hotfix
notes.notes:
Hello, Catalysts! Very small patch here, but this should fix a huge and VERY stubborn bug. Glad to have finally been able to hunt this one down.

We're still working on a pretty dang meaty content update and smoothing out the early game, but that's for another post...

GENERAL:

Fixed an issue where certain save files (i.e. friends list and floor tiles) would not load properly and be overwritten, if launched on a new device with cloud saves.

notes.title: v1.6c - Quest time hotfix, OoB Building fix
notes.notes:
Hello again! Another lil' hotfix. We noticed a lot of folk getting weird bugs where a "GUILD" quest would look like it just repeats endlessly without completing. It shouldn't do that now.

QUESTS:
-Fixed quests with a GUILD status getting stuck for absurd amounts of time.
-Fixed inaccuracies with quest timers that caused timers to appear to loop.

BUILDINGS:
-Fixed being able to place buildings waaaaaaaaaay out of bounds if your window was wide enough.

notes.title: v1.6a - Very small UI hotfix
notes.notes:
Whoops! I thought the lists were in the right order but they weren't. Now they are. Dun worry 'bout it. That's what these letter hotfixes are for.


 Fixed the Moons menu using an incorrect icon after gaining forbidden knowledge.

notes.title: v1.3c - V. small hotfix
notes.notes:
Hello! Mostly just pushing this out for the change in the Progression tab, but a couple other changes snuck their way in there.

PROGRESSION:

 Fixed a part of the tutorial appearing after you've already beaten the game


BUILDINGS:

 Certain roof decor (like string lights from the comet) should no longer sell items.


MENUS:

 Added a confirmation screen to the Reset Default Settings option.

notes.title: v1.2b hotfix - Pets weren't petting, folks had quills, it was crazy
notes.notes:
Hello again (again)! Here's another small hotfix to polish up v1.2 from earlier today.

MENUS:
-Fixed two different shrines having swapped icons.
-Building UIs are now hidden when placing one.
-Fixed the wardrobe's Pet changing button not actually giving you a pet.

ADVENTURERS:
-Fixed buildings attracting quill-wielding adventurers. (That's supposed to just be you!)

notes.title: v1.2a hotfix - Wardrobe crash fix, Boss 3 UI limits
notes.notes:
Heya! EXTREMELY small hotfix for something that was affecting a lot of folk.

MENUS:
-Fixed a crash when selecting a costume part in the wardrobe
-Fixed a visual bug on the filling bars UI of Boss 3's related thing.

notes.title: v1.1b Hotfix/QoL Update
notes.notes:
Hello, Settlers! This update improves some menu-related things as well as fixing some things with the Display Stands people are unlocking.

Importantly, though, adventurers can now spawn in more colors, too! Keep an eye out for their even worse fashion sense.

BUILDINGS:
-Nerfed Gazebos. Sorry! Reduced Level: 1 -> 0.5, Reduced AoE Effect: 30% -> 20%
-Fixed a specific music sheet building being on the wrong tab.
-Fixed some super weird menu behavior when replacing a building with a display stand.
-Fixed a crash when placing a blueprint of a display stand next to a shop.

MENUS:
-Updated the Logbook's icon to have a silver coin on it, to better convey that's where you do stuff with money.
-The Quests button on the main menu now shows how many quest slots are completed.
-The Quests button now only highlights when there's a completed quest you can actually pay for.
-The Logbook tab now highlights adventurers while making everything behind them more opaque.
-Added a back button to the menu associated with the display stand.

NPCS:
-NPCs now have a dimmed nametag when they have nothing to give you.
-Fixed an incorrect icon when an NPC gives you an item FOR REAL THIS TIME.

SAVE RESETS:
-Fixed a save reset bug in which certain town states wouldn't reset until the game restarts.
-Fixed a save reset bug in which the game would never actually save anything post-reset until the game restarts.

ALSO:
-Expanded the range of colors Adventurers can spawn with!

notes.title: v1.1a Hotfix Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Settlers! (that's you.)
Some UI updates and crash fixes on this one; if you got a crash after adding a lot of friends, you should be able to load your town again!
Also added an exit button on the main menu, so y'all fullscreen gamers have a way to escape this realm of torment.
Lastly, stamped out another potential tutorial softlock...well, okay, not "softlock", but it made things way more confusing than they needed to be.

BUILDINGS:
-Holding paint over a building now previews what it will look like.
-Fixed some buildings not recoloring with paint. (Banners, axe stump, and a guard tower)
-Fixed the last paint in the menu using the wrong color on the icon.

MENUS:
-Added an exit button on the sides of the main menu! You can just close the window, but this is good for fullscreen.
-Fixed a crash when picking up a monster quest while already holding a material.
-Popup windows now darken the background and prevent you from clicking on things below it before it's dismissed.
-You can no longer delete the tutorial quest until it's actually done. This fixes a sorta-softlock and a lot of confusion.

ALSO:
-Fixed a crash involving saving too many friends.
-Fixed an incorrect icon when a certain NPC gives you a flower.
-Fixed full town screenshots with Chroma Key enabled only having a chunk of the background being chroma key'd.
-Made the right side of town look less square-y with Chroma Key enabled.

notes.title: v1.1 - The "Game Actually Explains Things" Update
notes.notes:
Hello again! I really should have a name for you all, shouldn't I? Settlers? Eh, whatever.

Clarity is important! And as it turns out, trying to figure out how the game works without it actually telling you is pretty rough.
This patch should help a lot with onboarding; it explains how the game's basics actually work (using WORDS) and hopefully clears up some confusion about Quests in particular.

I'll still be looking at the new player experience after this! I'd hate to turn away players just because they aren't lucking into figuring out how things work.

Next up, I want to add a wardrobe that lets you save and load outfits for your little avatar. This felt more important, though.

Changes in v1.1:
TUTORIALS:
-The first card you get is now a basic tutorial! It explains how the game loop works (in english).
-The main menu now has a help button that re-opens the tutorial card. You can toggle this button off in the options menu if it's looking too patronizing.
-The tutorial card that explains time now includes a page about quests.
-The previously-first card should now be given by an NPC after the inn is placed.

QUESTS:
-Quests now say "CLOSED" instead of "EDITING" when not open, for better conveyance.
-The anteater mailman now lowers his arm and leaves ASAP after you take what he has for you. He's got places to be!

ALSO:
-Added several new adventurer cosmetics!
-Stealth-nerfed an item. You won't notice it.

notes.title: v1.0a Hotfix patch notes
notes.notes:
Hello! I hope you've all been enjoying Settlemoon so far!

I'll be hotfixing the game to take care of some crashes and other weird stuff as they come up! Hotfixes will just add a letter to the end of the version number; actual content updates will be v1.1.
You can check what version you're on by looking at the button for the Options menu.

Here's the changes for v1.0a:

MENUS:
-Fixed a crash when trying to pick a friend and backing out of the menu at the same time.
-The back button on menus now adapts to changing the window size without having to open another menu.

PROGRESSION:
-Fixed a softlock involving starting a quest before the tutorial gets there.
-Also added some extra failsafes if you ARE in that softlock; you'll have to delete the quest (drag it downwards) and re-open the menu first.
